# coderforge_network_rule (Resource)

A port forwarding rule from the host to a machine.

The platform identifies a rule by its whole tuple rather than by a handle, so every attribute forces replacement: there is no way to modify a rule in place, only to remove one and add another. The `id` is derived from the tuple, which is what makes `terraform import` work without looking anything up.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "coderforge_machine" "web" {
  name = "web01"
  cpu  = 2
  ram  = 4096
}

# Forward one host port to the machine.
resource "coderforge_network_rule" "http" {
  src_port  = "8080"
  dest_ip   = coderforge_machine.web.ip
  dest_port = "80"
  protocol  = "tcp"
}

# A range. Both sides must be the same width.
resource "coderforge_network_rule" "game_servers" {
  src_port  = "50000-50100"
  dest_ip   = coderforge_machine.web.ip
  dest_port = "50000-50100"
  protocol  = "udp"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `dest_ip` (String) Address traffic is forwarded to, usually a machine's `ip` attribute.
- `dest_port` (String) Guest port or range.
- `src_port` (String) Host port or range, as a string: `"8080"` or `"50000-50100"`. A range must be the same width as `dest_port`.

### Optional

- `protocol` (String) `tcp` or `udp`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Derived identifier, `<protocol>_<src_port>_<dest_ip>_<dest_port>` - for example `tcp_8080_192.168.56.10_80`.
- `managed_by` (String) Set when another resource owns this rule.
- `rid` (String) Cloud Builder registry id, when the rule carries one.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
# The id is derived from the rule itself:
#   <protocol>_<src_port>_<dest_ip>_<dest_port>
terraform import coderforge_network_rule.http tcp_8080_192.168.56.10_80
```
